name: Habitual Used To

1.definition: Presents a habitual situation or state as characteristic of a past period.

examples.form: The shop [used to close] at noon.

projection.target: Used to can describe a past state, as in Jo used to own it. The present counterpart use to does not express a parallel current habit in ordinary affirmative clauses.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Used to
curious.summary: Used to followed by a plain verb describes a habit or a state that belonged to a past period.
curious.body:
The shop used to close at noon tells us that closing at noon was the regular pattern at some earlier time. Used to can also describe a past state, as in Jo used to own it.

The present-tense counterpart, use to, doesn't parallel this by describing a current habit in an ordinary affirmative sentence.

examples.text: The shop [used to close] at noon.

curious.try: Say something about a place near you that has changed, starting with It used to ...

teacher.summary: Helps students use used to for past habits and states and see how it differs from the present.
teacher.explain: The pattern is used to plus a plain-form verb: The shop used to close at noon. It presents a habitual situation or state as characteristic of a past period, so it covers habits and states: Jo used to own it. This dictionary says the present counterpart use to does not express a parallel current habit in ordinary affirmative clauses. It treats it as a specialization of VP structure, related to the past tense, and marks the analysis as provisional.
teacher.terms: Often taught as the past habitual or used to + infinitive.

examples.text: The shop [used to close] at noon.

watch_for: A learner might use use to for a present habit in an affirmative sentence, when it doesn't parallel used to.
A learner might think used to covers only repeated actions, when it also covers states like owning.
teacher.activity: Students write two sentences with used to about how their town has changed, one a habit and one a state, then swap and decide which is which.

child.hook: How do you talk about how things were?
child.explain: Used to talks about how things were in the past. The shop used to close at noon.

examples.text: The shop [used to close] at noon.

child.play: Tell a partner two things that used to be true for you. Start each with I used to.

checked.note: Fixed: cut the unsupported 'the form for talking about how things were' (curious.body); child.explain no longer introduces 'state' undefined; child.play no longer asks children to sort habits from states; 'the entry' replaced by 'this dictionary'.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Habitual Used To." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/habitual-used-to-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, 5c11b28).
